rows: High strength is useful here but not universally better.
Workability and bond often matter more than Portland content.
Use Portland/lime where bond strength is critical.
Lower strength can be appropriate when units are soft or loads are low.
Type O, lime putty, or NHL mortar
Hard mortar can destroy soft historic units.
Petrographic analysis and original mortar match
"Match color" is not enough; match composition and vapor behavior.
Type S or M with air-entrained masonry cement
ASTM C476 fine or coarse grout
Grout is poured into cores; mortar belongs in joints.
Type N or S with smaller aggregate
Aggregate must pass through the joint without bridging.
Dry units steal water before bond develops.
